<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:lemma1}
  The local hull of a tiling of the plane with finite local complexity (e.g., a Penrose tiling) consists
  of all tilings built from the same set of local configurations.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
The topological space $X(\Lambda)$ is compact, and the translation action of $\mathbb{R}^d$ on $\Lambda$ lifts
  to a continuous translation action on $X(\Lambda)$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop_moody}
  The set $\{(t,0)_L \mid t\in\mathbb{R}^d\}$ is dense in the torus $(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)/\widetilde L$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop_s_b}
  There exists a \emph{torus parametrization of the local hull}, i.e., a continuous map
  \[\beta \colon X(\Lambda) \longrightarrow \mathbb T^{2d}\]
  such that
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $\beta$ is surjective;
    \item $\beta$ is injective almost everywhere (with respect to the Haar measure on the torus);
    \item $\beta(t+\Lambda') = \beta(\Lambda') + (t, 0)_L$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and all $\Lambda' \in X(\Lambda)$;
    \item $\beta(t + \Lambda) = (t, 0)_L$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
